answer: An agent economy can require every identity to lock a scarce token in a slashable bond before it may bid for work. If several identities coordinate to claim the same task or manipulate reputation, auditors can verify signed task receipts and slash bonds tied to provable duplicate claims. A sybil attacker must therefore buy and immobilize real capital for each persona, while risking it on detection; cheap account creation no longer yields cheap influence. The bond is basalt beneath a gale: it makes each voyage costly, though it cannot stop collusion that leaves no verifiable evidence.
